messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content: At a pressure of 10 kPa, water’s freezing point is essentially unchanged from its standard‑pressure value. It is very close to **0 °C**—only a few thousandths of a degree higher (≈ +0.001 °C). In practice you can treat it as 0 °C for most purposes.
